Refer to the Note 10 Income Tax.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">ASU 2025-05 "Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets"</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">In July 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-05 &#8220;Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets&#8221;, which introduces a practical expedient for estimating expected credit losses on current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under Topic 606, including those recognized in a business combination. The guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2025, including interim periods within those annual periods, with early adoption permitted. The Group adopted ASU 2025-05 early, effective January 1, 2025, and applied the guidance prospectively. In accordance with ASU 2025-05, the Group elected to apply the practical expedient provided in ASC 326-20-30-10C for current trade receivables arising from revenue transactions accounted for under ASC 606. Under this practical expedient, the Group assumes that current conditions as of the balance sheet date remain unchanged for the remaining life of the receivables when developing reasonable and supportable forecast.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="Duration_1_1_2025_To_12_31_2025_D7g9X38lIUyiy3R8Ai_LMg" name="nbis:EffectOfNewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyTextBlock" id="Tb_dnPGL52XX0KWRxBov9Ar5A" continuedAt="Tb_dnPGL52XX0KWRxBov9Ar5A_cont1" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 36pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Effect of Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements Not Yet Effective</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">ASU "2024-03, Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses"</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU &#8220;2024-03, Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses&#8221;, which requires more detailed disclosures, on an annual and interim basis, about specified categories of expenses (including employee compensation, depreciation, and amortization) included in certain expense captions presented on the consolidated statements of operations. This guidance, as further clarified through ASU 2025-01 &#8220;Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40)&#8221;, is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and for interim periods within fiscal years<b style="font-weight:bold;"> </b><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;">beginning after December 15, 2027.  Therefore, for the Group, the guidance will be effective for the year ending December 31, 2027, and for interim periods beginning January 1, 2028. Early adoption is permitted. Upon adoption, the guidance can be applied either prospectively or retrospectively. The Group is currently evaluating the impact this amended guidance may have on its consolidated financial statements.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">ASU 2025-06 "Intangibles-Goodwill and Other-Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software&#8221;</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06 &#8220;Intangibles-Goodwill and Other-Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software&#8221;, which clarifies and simplifies the capitalization guidance for internal-use software by removing references to sequential development stages and clarifying that capitalization begins when management has authorized and committed to funding the software project and it is probable the project will be completed and the software will be used as intended, considering any significant uncertainty in development activities. The guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods within those annual periods. Therefore, for the Group, the guidance will be effective for the year ending December 31, 2028. Early adoption is permitted. Upon adoption, the guidance may be applied prospectively, retrospectively, or on a modified retrospective basis, including for in-process projects. The Group is currently evaluating the impact this amended guidance may have on its consolidated financial statements.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">ASU 2025-11 "Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow-Scope Improvements"</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-11 &#8220;Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow-Scope Improvements&#8221;, which clarifies interim disclosure requirements and the applicability of Topic 270. The guidance will be effective for interim periods beginning January 1, 2028. Therefore, for the Group, the guidance will be effective for interim reporting periods beginning January 1, 2028, and will be reflected in the consolidated financial statements for the year ending December 31, 2028. Early adoption is permitted. NET INCOME/(LOSS) PER SHARE</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">Basic net income/(loss) per Class A and Class B ordinary share from continuing and discontinued operations for the years ended December&#160;31, 2023, 2024 and 2025 is computed on the basis of the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding using the two-class method. Basic net income/(loss) from continuing and discontinued operations and per share is computed using the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period and including vested restricted share units and shares to be delivered as part of the restructuring of the Company&#8217;s convertible notes in June 2022. Diluted net income/(loss) per ordinary share from continuing and discontinued operations is computed using the dilutive effect of Share-Based Awards calculated using the &#8220;treasury stock&#8221; method and the dilutive effect of convertible debt under the if-converted method. Transactions resulting in businesses being classified as discontinued operations are described in Note 3.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The computation of the diluted net income/(loss) per Class A share from continuing and discontinued operations assumes the conversion of Class B shares, while the diluted net income/(loss) per Class B share from continuing and discontinued operations does not assume the conversion of those shares. The net income/(loss) per share from continuing and discontinued operations amounts are the same for Class A and Class B shares because the holders of each class are legally entitled to equal per share distributions whether through dividends or liquidation. In compliance with ASC 260-10-45-18 the Group uses loss from continuing operations as the control number in determining whether those potential ordinary shares are dilutive or antidilutive. ("Toloka Group") of additional stock to third-party investors and a restructuring of the capital stock of Toloka Group into both voting and nonvoting common and preferred shares, as result of which the Company&#8217;s voting interest was reduced to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_pure_K_a6MVGvo020dBhQ3gfFag" contextRef="Duration_5_2_2025_To_5_2_2025_us-gaap_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis_us-gaap_DiscontinuedOperationsDisposedOfBySaleMember_us-gaap_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis_nbis_TolokaGroupIncMember_UYqhXgRVyUG8DJUjnXaTPA" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:PercentageOfOwnershipInterestRetainedAfterDisposal" scale="-2" id="Narr_yS37wYHrEk-T4zhYpl6hPQ">49</ix:nonFraction>%. Consequently, Toloka Group was deconsolidated from the Company&#8217;s financial statements, and the Company's retained share in Toloka was reclassified as an equity method investment under ASC 323 for the investment in common stock, while the investment in preferred stock was accounted for under ASC 321 using the measurement alternative. The Toloka Deconsolidation represents a strategic transaction aimed at enhancing the Group&#8217;s focus on its core AI infrastructure business while allowing Toloka to operate independently. The transaction qualifies as a "strategic shift" under ASC 205-20, requiring discontinued operations reporting, as Toloka constituted a significant business line for the Company.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The deconsolidation was accounted for in accordance with ASC 810, and the Company recognized a gain as the difference between the fair value of the retained investment (common and preferred stock) and the carrying amount of the assets and liabilities deconsolidated. Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">In October 2025, Avride issued a Simple Agreement for Future Equity (&#8220;SAFE&#8221;) to SMB Holding Corporation (&#8220;SMB&#8221;) in exchange for cash consideration of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="Duration_10_1_2025_To_10_31_2025_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_nbis_AvrideHoldingIncMember_1196LpneYkivqNcIXAEvpw" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" In connection with this arrangement, Avride also granted SMB a contingent right to receive an additional SAFE with a principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="Duration_10_1_2025_To_10_31_2025_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_nbis_AvrideHoldingIncMember_1196LpneYkivqNcIXAEvpw" decimals="-6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:ContingentRightAdditionalSafePrincipalAmount" scale="6" id="Narr_56F-zv_2aEmgq0iF5Y9i2g">75</ix:nonFraction> million upon achievement of specified operational and financing milestones (the &#8220;Tranche Right&#8221;). A SAFE is a freestanding financial instrument that provides the holder with the right to receive a variable number of Avride&#8217;s equity shares upon certain future events. Under the terms of the SAFE, upon a qualifying equity financing the SAFE automatically converts into preferred stock at a price equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_pure_K_a6MVGvo020dBhQ3gfFag" contextRef="Duration_10_1_2025_To_10_31_2025_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_nbis_AvrideHoldingIncMember_1196LpneYkivqNcIXAEvpw" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:SafeConversionPercentageOfPricePerSharePaid" scale="-2" id="Narr_RYt5LU9oskuG4BMqarchfw">80</ix:nonFraction>% of the price per share paid by new investors. Upon a liquidity or dissolution event, the holder is entitled to receive the greater of the original purchase amount or the amount otherwise payable upon conversion. The Tranche Right represents a conditional obligation to issue an additional SAFE for a fixed purchase amount if the specified milestones are achieved. Both the SAFE and the Tranche Right are classified as liabilities in accordance with ASC 480, &#8220;<i style="font-style:italic;">Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity&#8221;</i>, as they may require settlement through the issuance of a variable number of shares for a predominantly fixed monetary amount or, in certain circumstances, through the transfer of assets. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The SAFE liability and the Tranche Right liability are initially recorded at fair value in an amount equal to proceeds received and subsequently remeasured to fair value at each reporting date, with changes in fair value recognized in other income / (loss), net (Note 6). As of December 31, 2025, the fair value of the SAFE and the Tranche Right liability was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2025_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_nbis_AvrideHoldingIncMember_kFQHIpOgNUio0gtLJabSVQ" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:SimpleAgreementForFutureEquityInstrumentsFairValue" scale="6" id="Narr_58MUPgzWMEa6hTtZLncU1w">101.1</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2025_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_nbis_AvrideHoldingIncMember_kFQHIpOgNUio0gtLJabSVQ" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:ContingentRightLiability" scale="6" id="Narr_-hUAe1O1ZECo5jN4-xaArA">1.6</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Government grant</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">In 2025, the Group received formal approval from the Israeli Innovation Authority for a government grant to support the establishment and operation of an AI large-model training laboratory in Israel for the amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2025_srt_RangeAxis_srt_MaximumMember_bFbUVmCmmkmgwUAAlOwxwA" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceAwardAmount" scale="6" id="Narr_dLRUlNkthEKy6iUa9_a2WQ">54.1</ix:nonFraction>. Under the program, the Group is required to deploy and operate advanced AI computing infrastructure and provide eligible Israeli industry and research institutions with multi-year access to those services.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The grant provided in 2025 covers eligible costs incurred from May 2025 through April 2026. In addition, the Group is eligible to maintain its participation and is required to continue meeting the program&#8217;s operational and service requirements for a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="Duration_1_1_2025_To_12_31_2025_D7g9X38lIUyiy3R8Ai_LMg" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" name="nbis:GovernmentAssistanceOperationalCommitmentDuration" id="Narr_LFBEhz2wXEGsSjbO597P9w">three-year</ix:nonNumeric> period through April 2028.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The grant is provided in the form of cash reimbursements for eligible expenditures. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Group received cash installments totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2025_To_12_31_2025_D7g9X38lIUyiy3R8Ai_LMg" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:ProceedsFromGovernmentGrant" scale="6" id="Narr_o9P4xOfjfkWS1iw1gwuOeQ">44.4</ix:nonFraction>.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The Group has determined that the grant contains both asset-related and income-related components and accounts for each portion separately based on the nature of the underlying expenditures.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p></ix:continuation></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:27.35pt;min-height:36pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">F-33</p></div></div></div>

FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">Fair value measurements are determined in accordance with ASC 820, Fair Value Measurements, which defines fair value as an exit price that represents the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. ASC 820 establishes a framework for fair value measurements and includes a three-tier hierarchy that prioritizes the use of observable inputs for fair value measurements:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:31.5pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 36pt;">Level&#160;1&#8212;observable inputs that reflect quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:31.5pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 36pt;">Level&#160;2&#8212;inputs other than quoted prices included within Level&#160;1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly; and</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:31.5pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 36pt;">Level&#160;3&#8212; unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activities.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Investments measured at fair value on a recurring basis</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The Group's financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis include investments in cash and cash equivalents, including money market funds, accounts receivables, other assets (except prepayments and deferred expenses), trade accounts payables, investments in non-marketable equity securities, equity method investments, financial assets and financial liabilities from discontinued operations and convertible debt. Cash, accounts receivable, and trade accounts payables are stated at their carrying value, which approximates fair value due to the short-term nature of these items except for the fair value of the convertible debt (Note 12).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">Money market funds (presented as part of cash and cash equivalents) are measured at fair value and classified as Level 1 within the fair value hierarchy, as their valuation is based on quoted prices for identical assets in active markets or on inputs derived from quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets. As of December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, money market funds measured at fair value totaled $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2024_us-gaap_CashAndCashEquivalentsAxis_us-gaap_MoneyMarketFundsMember_us-gaap_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaap_FairValueInputsLevel1Member_us-gaap_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_us-gaap_FairValueMeasurementsRecurringMember_P23Q7RlHDUiOLSZRFvCllQ" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" id="Narr_4Ds-JKqwoEyBfmXze_2NPQ">500.4</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2025_us-gaap_CashAndCashEquivalentsAxis_us-gaap_MoneyMarketFundsMember_us-gaap_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaap_FairValueInputsLevel1Member_us-gaap_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_us-gaap_FairValueMeasurementsRecurringMember_mdIDIOB6GEykUJrFPHpi_Q" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" id="Narr_vz-5ab6QSEWIk0shsKhjZg">1,770.9</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Avride SAFE liability and Tranche Right liability</i></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The SAFE liability and the Tranche Right liability are initially recorded at fair value in amount equal to proceeds received and subsequently remeasured to fair value at each reporting date, with changes in fair value recognized in other income / (loss), net. Accordingly, these instruments are classified within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy. The Group&#8217;s principal operations are in the Netherlands and the United States, with a growing data center and infrastructure footprint across multiple international regions, including Finland, France, the United Kingdom, Iceland and Israel.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">The global macroeconomic environment continues to be characterized by significant uncertainty. The technology and AI infrastructure sectors have been particularly affected by the evolving trade policy landscape in 2025, shifting AI chip export control frameworks, and ongoing trade tensions between major economies. Supply chain constraints affecting the procurement of high-performance GPUs and related semiconductor components remain a key operational challenge, driven by strong global demand for AI infrastructure that continues to outpace available capacity. Regulatory developments impacting the AI and data center sectors have accelerated, including the phased implementation of the European Union&#8217;s Artificial Intelligence Act, emerging data center energy efficiency and sustainability reporting requirements under the EU Energy Efficiency Directive, and the EU&#8217;s proposed Cloud and AI Development Act. Changes in interest rates, persistent inflationary pressures&#8212;exacerbated by tariff-related cost increases instability in the global credit markets, geopolitical conflicts in Europe and the Middle East, data center energy procurement and power grid capacity constraints, and related market uncertainty remain relevant factors. While global demand for AI computing infrastructure has driven substantial investment and growth across the sector, the Group is exposed to the risks of macroeconomic slowdowns, shifts in technology spending patterns, and the potential impacts of further regulatory or trade policy changes. The Group will continue to actively monitor and respond accordingly to the macroeconomic environment.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;">Following the completion of the Divestment, the Group continues to have no exposure to the risks and uncertainties associated with the operations of the Divested Businesses. As of December 31, 2025, none of the Group&#8217;s current subsidiaries are restricted from remitting funds in the form of cash dividends or loans.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 6pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Loss recovery</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:36pt;margin:6pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">During the quarter ended December 31, 2025, certain equipment with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="Unit_Standard_USD_mgu3S3_frUmT0MCXjbyKtQ" contextRef="Duration_10_1_2025_To_12_31_2025_L6UBYQnFEUi_kv8p01WX5Q" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="nbis:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentLostInTransit" scale="6" id="Narr_6kW_dTyOQ0Kgiubzj8usJQ">43.6</ix:nonFraction> was lost in transit. The equipment was fully insured, and the Group has submitted a claim to the insurer and is pursuing recovery under its existing insurance policy. At this stage, the Group cannot make any predictions about the exact timing and likelihood of recovery.</p></ix:continuation><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:27.35pt;min-height:36pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">F-45</p></div></div></div>
